MSFT.rationale: Microsoft presents a solid fundamental picture with strong revenue growth (+18.3% YoY in Q3 FY2026), robust AI business momentum ($37B annual run rate, +123% YoY), and a fortress balance sheet (net cash of ~$38B). Azure's 40% growth and expanding operating margins (46.3%) demonstrate durable competitive positioning. However, the stock is not a screaming bargain — at 30.5x trailing P/E it sits mid-range of its 25-43x 12-month window, and massive $190B capex plans are compressing free cash flow and gross margins (67.6%, lowest since 2022). The QoQ EPS decline of -17.2% (Q3 vs Q2) reflects some earnings volatility. Valuation is fair-to-slightly-cheap vs its own recent history (P/E was 37-42x a year ago), providing modest upside. Near-term catalysts include the upcoming Q4 FY2026 earnings (July 29) where Azure is guided to accelerate beyond 40%, and the Build conference AI announcements, but these are partially priced in given the recent 5%+ rally on the $37B AI run rate disclosure. Regulatory headwinds (FTC probe expansion) and insider selling (Gates Foundation fully divested, multiple executives selling) temper conviction.
key_factors: Strong revenue growth: +18.3% YoY to $82.9B in Q3 FY2026, with Azure growing 40% YoY
AI business at $37B annual run rate (+123% YoY) with Copilot at 20M paid enterprise seats
Fortress balance sheet: $78.3B cash vs $40.3B debt, net cash ~$38B
Valuation mid-range: P/E 30.5x vs 12-month range of 25-43x, cheaper than year-ago 37-42x
Margin pressure from $190B 2026 capex plan: gross margin fell to 67.6%, FCF compressed
QoQ EPS decline of -17.2% (Q3 $4.27 vs Q2 $5.16) showing some earnings volatility
Regulatory risk: FTC expanded antitrust probe into cloud, AI, and bundling practices
Q4 FY2026 guidance: revenue $86.7-87.8B, Azure growth expected to accelerate beyond 40%
Insider selling: Gates Foundation fully divested, multiple executives selling shares
Copilot monetization still early: only 4.4% of 450M M365 base converted
